newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-CELTIC TELL VAN HOOYDONK TO GROW UP.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CELTIC TELL VAN HOOYDONK TO GROW UP.

text.p: Scottish premier division Glasgow Celtic have told disgruntled Dutch striker Pierre Van Hooydonk to grow up and warned their patience with him is growing thin.
Van Hooydonk, who scored 26 league goals for Celtic last season, is seeking a pay rise and is reported to have threatened to leave Parkhead if his demands are not met.
Celtic have said they will pay him more but only if he agrees now to extend his current contract, which still has 21 months to run.

"Pierre van Hooydonk has scored excellent goals for Celtic, however no one is bigger than the club and the player must follow the same rules as everyone else," Celtic chairman Fergus McCann told a news conference on Monday.

"The manager has shown considerable patience and leniency with the player and now it's time for the player to decide whether he wants to grow up, tell the truth and be a Celtic player and all that that involves.
"The players knows that the club is willing to increase his earnings immediately but only in return for an extension to his existing contract.
McCann said Van Hooydonk had refused to take part in a number of obligatory club events such as testimonial matches or speak to the media.
"There have also been other incidents of a commercial and charitable nature where the player has refused to give his time, despite his contractual obligations," McGann said.
Van Hooydonk was left out of the Celtic side which lost 2-0 to city rivals Rangers on Saturday.
